concepts.name: Agrochemical Overuse: Fertilizers and Soil Degradation
key_dimensions: Mechanism of nitrogen/phosphorus accumulation and eutrophication linkage
Difference between organic fertilizers and synthetic fertilizers in soil impact
NPK imbalance and its long-term effect on soil microbiome and pH
UPSC trap: Fertilizer subsidy policy vs. soil health — conflicting government priorities

concepts.name: Pesticides and Persistent Organic Pollutants (POPs) in Soil
key_dimensions: Biomagnification vs. bioaccumulation — distinction in soil context
Stockholm Convention on POPs: banned substances and India's obligations
Organochlorines (DDT, Endosulfan) vs. organophosphates — persistence comparison
UPSC trap: Endosulfan ban controversy — Centre vs. State (Kerala) conflict

concepts.name: Industrial Effluents and Heavy Metal Contamination
key_dimensions: Key heavy metals: Lead, Cadmium, Mercury, Chromium, Arsenic — sources and threshold limits
Difference between heavy metal contamination and radioactive contamination in soil
Tannery, mining, and electroplating industries as primary point sources
UPSC trap: Phytoremediation vs. bioremediation — mechanism and applicable contaminant types

concepts.name: Solid Waste Dumping and Leachate Formation
key_dimensions: Municipal Solid Waste (MSW) Rules 2016 — provisions for landfill siting and leachate management
Leachate composition and its pathway to soil and groundwater contamination
Difference between sanitary landfill, open dumping, and bioreactor landfill
UPSC trap: Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) under Plastic Waste Rules — link to soil pollution prevention

concepts.name: Mining Activities as a Cause of Soil Pollution
key_dimensions: Acid Mine Drainage (AMD) — mechanism and affected regions in India (Jharkhand, Odisha)
Overburden dumping vs. tailings — distinction and soil impact
MMDR Act provisions vs. environmental safeguards — regulatory gap
UPSC trap: Forest clearance for mining vs. soil conservation — overlapping jurisdiction of MoEFCC

concepts.name: Sewage Sludge Application in Agriculture
key_dimensions: Nutrient value of sewage sludge vs. risk of pathogen and heavy metal introduction
Difference between treated sludge (biosolids) and untreated sewage irrigation
India's gap: Absence of dedicated biosolids reuse regulation unlike EU Sewage Sludge Directive
UPSC trap: Wastewater irrigation — simultaneous cause of soil enrichment AND soil pollution

concepts.name: Plastic Waste and Microplastic Contamination of Soil
key_dimensions: Fragmentation pathway: macroplastics → microplastics → nanoplastics in soil
Impact on soil porosity, water retention, and earthworm activity
Mulch films and single-use plastics in agriculture as primary vectors
UPSC trap: Biodegradable vs. oxo-degradable plastics — oxo-degradable plastics accelerate microplastic formation

concepts.name: Radioactive Contamination of Soil
key_dimensions: Sources: Nuclear power plants, uranium mining, medical/industrial waste improper disposal
Half-life concept — why radioactive soil pollution is uniquely long-term
Atomic Energy Act 1962 and AERB regulations — regulatory framework
UPSC trap: Radioactive contamination is NOT covered under Environment Protection Act — falls under Atomic Energy Act

concepts.name: Acid Rain and Soil Acidification
key_dimensions: Mechanism: SOx, NOx → H2SO4, HNO3 deposition → pH reduction in soil
Impact on nutrient leaching (calcium, magnesium loss) and aluminium toxicity release
Difference between soil acidification from acid rain vs. from fertilizer use (ammonium-based)
UPSC trap: Acid rain is a secondary pollutant phenomenon — link to transboundary air pollution

concepts.name: Urbanization and Construction Activity as Soil Pollutants
key_dimensions: Sealing of soil (impervious surfaces) — loss of soil functions vs. chemical pollution distinction
Construction and demolition (C&D) waste — heavy metals and asbestos contamination
C&D Waste Management Rules 2016 — provisions and implementation gaps
UPSC trap: Soil sealing is considered a form of soil degradation/pollution but is often omitted in standard definitions

concepts.name: E-Waste Dismantling and Informal Recycling
key_dimensions: Toxic substances released: Lead, Mercury, Cadmium, Brominated flame retardants
E-Waste (Management) Rules 2022 — EPR framework and its soil pollution prevention angle
Informal sector in India (Dharavi, Moradabad) — ground reality vs. regulatory intent
UPSC trap: E-waste rules cover producers/importers but informal dismantlers remain outside regulatory ambit

concepts.name: Deforestation and Loss of Soil Organic Matter
key_dimensions: Mechanism: Canopy removal → erosion, leaching, loss of humus → soil degradation
Difference between soil pollution (introduction of contaminants) and soil degradation (loss of quality) — definitional trap
Link to carbon sequestration loss and climate feedback
UPSC trap: Deforestation causes soil degradation primarily, but burning for land clearing introduces PAHs — making it a pollution cause too

concepts.name: Oil Spills and Petroleum Hydrocarbon Contamination
key_dimensions: Terrestrial oil spills from pipelines, storage tanks, and vehicle fuel leaks
Total Petroleum Hydrocarbons (TPH) — impact on soil aeration and microbial activity
Bioremediation using hydrocarbon-degrading bacteria — specific application
UPSC trap: Oil pollution is predominantly discussed in marine context — soil dimension is frequently overlooked

concepts.name: Pharmaceutical and Emerging Contaminants in Soil
key_dimensions: Pathway: Veterinary drugs (antibiotics in livestock manure) → soil → antibiotic resistance gene (ARG) spread
Endocrine-disrupting chemicals (EDCs) — definition, sources, and soil entry routes
India's pharmaceutical manufacturing hubs (Hyderabad) and effluent discharge — Patancheru case
UPSC trap: Antibiotic resistance from soil is a One Health issue — intersection of environment, animal health, and human health

concepts.name: Irrigation with Contaminated Water (Wastewater Irrigation)
key_dimensions: Prevalence in peri-urban agriculture in India — heavy metal and pathogen accumulation
FAO guidelines on safe use of wastewater in agriculture vs. Indian practice gap
Difference between treated wastewater reuse (positive) and raw sewage irrigation (polluting)
UPSC trap: Same practice (wastewater irrigation) can be framed as a solution (water conservation) or a cause (soil pollution) — context-dependent

concepts.name: Soil Health Card Scheme and National Soil Policy Framework
key_dimensions: Soil Health Card Scheme (2015) — parameters tested, institutional mechanism, limitations
National Land Degradation Neutrality (LDN) target under UNCCD — India's commitment
Difference between Soil Health Card and soil pollution monitoring — SHC does NOT test for heavy metals/POPs routinely
UPSC trap: India lacks a standalone National Soil Pollution Act — soil pollution governed under EPA 1986 and state rules fragmentarily

concepts.name: Salinization and Waterlogging as Anthropogenic Soil Degradation Causes
key_dimensions: Secondary salinization from over-irrigation — mechanism and affected Indian regions (Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan)
Difference between primary salinization (natural) and secondary salinization (anthropogenic)
Waterlogging reducing soil oxygen and triggering anaerobic decomposition — link to methane and soil toxicity
UPSC trap: Salinization is categorized as soil degradation under UNCCD but can also be framed as soil pollution when caused by industrial effluents

concepts.name: Regulatory and Institutional Framework for Soil Pollution in India
key_dimensions: Environment Protection Act 1986 — soil pollution coverage: general vs. specific
CPCB and SPCB roles in soil pollution monitoring — gaps in mandated standards
Comparison: India vs. EU Soil Framework Directive — India's absence of dedicated soil law
UPSC trap: The Water Act 1974 and Air Act 1981 have dedicated frameworks, but NO equivalent dedicated Soil Protection Act exists in India — frequently tested gap
